verdict: M174 independently passes its exact-SHA directed VCS/SVA and all precommitted standalone logic-only DC bounds. The same-cycle done-to-next-token handshake removes the M171 interface bubble under always-ready assumptions, so the M173 128-bit isolated-token ratio is a defensible M174 analytic continuous-frontend boundary, but it is not an RTL-measured, memory-composed, complete-FC2, FFN, physical, or system speedup.

r1.finding: The expected TCL digest recorded in preflight has 62 hexadecimal characters and does not equal the observed 64-character SHA-256. No DC reports were produced and the run is not used.

r1b.finding: DC reports exist and numerically agree with r1c, but the runner did not issue RUN_COMPLETE and did not preserve a detailed post-DC failure reason. The review does not promote or cite r1b as admitted evidence.

m171_to_m174_recovery.baseline_provenance_finding: The 0.3385 ns arithmetic is correct only against the M174 contract's declared 0.0012 ns baseline. The sealed M171 timing_setup.rpt and qor.rpt expose 0.0000 ns and 0.00 ns, respectively, not 0.0012 ns. Use 43-level recovery unqualified; label setup recovery as 0.3397 ns report-to-report or preserve evidence for the higher-precision 0.0012 ns baseline.

m173_m174_cycle_semantic_audit.qualification: This carries M173's exact-payload recurrence into the reviewed M174 handshake semantics. It is analytic and assumes immediate 128-bit scan delivery plus always-ready group and done consumers; the 120 frozen payloads were not replayed through M174 RTL.

P1: Replay representative and edge-case slices of the 120 frozen payloads through M174 RTL and compare every emitted descriptor plus token boundary against an independent software oracle.
Build a matched 96-bit hierarchical frontend and include bitmap-delivery cost; M173 shows 128-bit buys only 1.075677x K4 isolated throughput over 96-bit for 33.333 percent more bitmap width.
